messages.subject: jointprior
messages.body_plain:
Hey,

I have some problems in understanding what deal does in the function
"jointprior" and "jointdisc" respectively.

let´s say I have a data.frame (data attached below) with 3 variables.
"Treatment", "Rec" (Recurrence) and "Subtype."  To get an idea what´s
going on I did:

#------------------------------------
library(debug) # nice debug function for R
mtrace(jointprior)
mtrace(jointdisc)
#------------------------------------


#------------------------------------
mydata = data.frame with some data for "Treatment","Rec" and "Subtype"
<-- discrete
nw = network(mydata)
localprob(nw,"Treatment") = c(0.5,0.5) 
localprob(nw,"Subtype") = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.3) 
localprob(nw,"Rec") = c(0.4,0.6) 
#------------------------------------

#get jointprior
nw.prior <- jointprior(nw)

    #--> jumps to the function "jointdisc"

#for each node:{
   #first node / loop
    >...
    >...

    Pn <- node$prob      # which is --> localprob(nw,"Treatment") =
c(0.5,0.5) 
    bigPn <- array(Pn, jDim)     # with jDim =  c(2,3,2)
    #bigPn is now an array where every value is 0.5

    #second node / loop
         Pn <- node$prob      # which is now -->
localprob(nw,"Subtype") = c(02, 0.5, 0.3) 
         bigPn <- array(Pn, jDim)     # with jDim =  c(2,3,2)

    #output for bigPn[1,,] is:
    #      rec.no rec.yes
    # 1    0.2     0.2
    # 2    0.3     0.3
    # 3    0.5     0.5
        #-> I don´t understand what´s going on her   
            # should´nt it be
            #          rec.no                     rec.yes
            # 1    0.08 (=0.4*0.2)        0.12 (=0.6*0.2)
            # 2    0.2   (=0.4*0.5)        0.3   (=0.6*0.5)
            # 3    0.12  (=0.4*0.3)       0.18  (=0.6*0.3)
>...
>...
#------------------------------------

I can not interpret the jointprior of "bigPn." when I compute the
jointprior by hand I get completely different results.


Does someone have an inside into "deal" and the way how the
jointpriors are calculated?

Thanks in advance
Peter
